definitions.explanation: The period when something is at its most flourishing, intense, or active state. Used for seasons, popularity, careers, or physical condition.
The breeding season or mating period for animals, especially cats and dogs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{盛|さか}り⟦だ→だ：noentry⟧。
examples.english: The cherry blossoms are now at their peak.

examples.japanese: ⟦{働|はたら}き→働く：00503_hataraku⟧{盛|ざか}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{年齢|ねんれい}→年齢：01490_nenrei⟧⟦だ→だ：noentry⟧。
examples.english: He is at the prime working age.
examples.notes: [Note: 働き盛り is a compound meaning 'prime working years']

examples.japanese: ⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{盛|さか}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついて、⟦{毎晩|まいばん}→毎晩：00967_maiban⟧⟦{鳴|な}いている→鳴く：04388_naku⟧。
examples.english: The cat is in heat and meows every night.
examples.notes: [Note: 盛りがつく means 'to go into heat']

notes:
USAGE: Most commonly appears in compound forms:
・〜{盛|ざか}り ({働|はたら}き{盛|ざか}り - prime working age, {食|た}べ{盛|ざか}り - age when one eats a lot)
・{盛|さか}りを{過|す}ぎる (to be past one's prime)
・{盛|さか}りがつく (to go into heat)

PATTERNS:
・今が盛りだ (to be at the peak now)
・盛りの + noun (at the height of...)

WRITING: Usually written with kanji 盛り. The reading changes to ざかり in compounds.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{最盛期|さいせいき} (peak period - more formal)
・{全盛|ぜんせい} (heyday, golden age)
・{絶頂|ぜっちょう} (climax, peak)
